Within the item view's context the binding is the member (a Discourse.User), which has no `automatic` property — `automatic` lives on the group model. Unlike the add-members block, which is correctly guarded with `{{#unless automatic}}` at the controller level, the member list rendering path has no such guard passed down, so the remove link can render for automatic groups wher

parsed_response.reasoning: In group.hbs the member list is rendered via `{{each member in members itemView="group-member"}}` and the item template group_member.hbs uses `{{#unless automatic}}<a class='remove' {{action "removeMember" member}}>...`. Within the item view's context the binding is the member (a Discourse.User), which has no `automatic` property — `automatic` lives on the group model. Unlike the add-members block, which is correctly guarded with `{{#unless automatic}}` at the controller level, the member list rendering path has no such guard passed down, so the remove link can render for automatic groups where the controller's `automatic` isn't reachable from the member context. The diff shows no mechanism (e.g., a controller/view exposing `automatic` to the item view) that would make the binding resolve. This is plausible from the diff, though Ember context resolution details make full certainty limited.
